content.title: Character Card Verification | Evidence Confirmation
content.summary: Fixed character cards appear repeatedly, using four different types of evidence—posture, operation, gait, and facial features—to verify the same identity.

quick_start.input_format: Character + fixed identity card + 4 distinct proofs (posture/action/gait/facial detail) + final live-action identity hold
quick_start.recommended_input: The ceramic service robot is repeatedly compared with fixed character cards to verify its standing posture proportions, tray operation, corridor gait, and facial lighting expressions, culminating in a hero freeze-frame in a real-life museum scene.
required_anchors: The same identity remains stable across shots
The four types of evidence serve different functions
At the end, enter a real scene to complete verification
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Fixed character cards appear repeatedly, using four different types of evidence: posture, operation, gait and face to verify the same identity.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Use one fixed identity board as a recurring visual checkpoint between four different live-scene proofs: silhouette and pose, small performance action, locomotion and face-level detail. Keep the board layout stable while camera scale and environment vary, then remove or subordinate the board so the verified live subject owns the final hero composition.

invariants.rule: Establish the identity board and live subject together before major action.
invariants.ablation_failure: A hidden reference cannot function as visible evidence.

invariants.rule: Return to the same board layout between distinct live proofs.
invariants.purpose: Makes each action a new identity check.
invariants.ablation_failure: A changing board destroys the reference baseline.

invariants.rule: Each live proof must test a different identity dimension.
invariants.ablation_failure: Repeated face close-ups do not prove gait or silhouette.

invariants.rule: Keep defining proportions and markers continuous across board and scene.
invariants.purpose: Preserves subject identity through camera changes.
invariants.ablation_failure: Marker drift breaks the verification mechanism.

invariants.rule: End on the verified live subject rather than a board-only frame.
invariants.purpose: Converts evidence into a satisfying hero payoff.
invariants.ablation_failure: A board-only ending feels like documentation, not completion.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original subject or system whose identity remains stable.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One visible variable that changes in countable causal stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained behavior rule that makes the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: A coherent information order that does not copy source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: One clean physical or graphic consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: A new hierarchy of diegetic cues supporting state changes.

anti_copy_exclusions: blonde anime cowgirl with black hat and sunglasses
Route 66 sunset and vintage muscle car
the NOVA character sheet layout and source end card
